newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tosoh Corp to raise ethylene capacity by 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tosoh Corp to raise ethylene capacity by 19 pct.

text.p: Tosoh Corp said on Friday it would build a new naphtha cracker at its Yokkaichi plant in central Japan by autumn 1998, boosting the firm's annual ethylene output capacity by 85,000 tonnes to 527,000 tonnes.
The expansion project will cost an estimated $7 billion yen.
"We have decided to carry out the project to meet the growing ethylene demand at our plants," a company spokesman said.
Tosoh started up a 300,000-tonne-a-year vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) plant in western Japan last year, raising the firm's annual ethylene consumption by 150,000 tonnes.
The VCM plant's output capacity will eventually be increased to 500,000 tonnes, the spokesman said.
Currently, Tosoh purchases about 400,000 tonnes of ethylene per year, mainly from other domestic petrochemical manufacturers, while producing some 420,000 tonnes at its own facilities.
